stepVerbs.expect: text must be visible within 20 s, else the take stops
stepVerbs.click: move the cursor to the element (role + name, or text), outline it, click
stepVerbs.clickIfPresent: click only when the element exists (optional wizard steps)
stepVerbs.hover: move the cursor to the element and hold
stepVerbs.type: type text (into a placeholder or the focused element)
stepVerbs.waitTurn: wait until the agent turn ends (no Stop button); the edit speed-ramps this span
stepVerbs.ensureOption: open a combobox and pick an option only when it does not already show it
stepVerbs.cut: hard cut in the edit; nothing is recorded across it

shots.vo: Cursor in SpecWithCode: plan, build, review.

card.title: Cursor in SpecWithCode
card.subtitle: Plan, build and review one task. The plan stays in your repo.

shots.vo: In your repo, run specweave init with the Cursor adapter. It adds AGENTS.md and eleven SpecWeave skills.
shots.stepChip: In your repo: specweave init . --quick --adapter cursor

showLines: ✓ 11 skills installed as sw-* in .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/
steps.elide: dim … row between and after the two lines

shots.vo: Open SpecWithCode, then Settings, Providers. Cursor is off by default: click Add provider, pick Cursor, click Next twice, then Add instance.
shots.stepChip: Settings → Providers → + → Cursor → Next → Next → Add instance

steps.name: Account: Demo Mac
steps.note: sidebar footer; opens the account menu

steps.name: Providers
steps.note: settings nav; route /settings/providers; only Codex and Claude rows show

steps.name: Add provider
steps.note: the + at the right of the Providers header

steps.text: Add an account or configure a provider on Demo Mac.
steps.note: dialog "Add provider", steps Provider, Identity, Config

steps.name: Cursor
steps.note: the ACP Registry list below also has an "Add Cursor" button; do not use it
Identity step: Label, Instance ID, Accent color; leave as is

steps.text: This driver has no required configuration.
Sign in with Cursor or add CURSOR_API_KEY
steps.note: the new Cursor row reads Not authenticated until sign-in

shots.vo: Click Sign in, then Open browser, and approve. It runs on the Cursor SDK, so you don't need the Cursor CLI.
shots.stepChip: Cursor → Account: Sign in → Open browser · no Cursor CLI needed
shots.verified: steps up to Open browser rendered on 0.2.6; the steps after the browser hand-off are not verified (no sign-in was possible)

steps.name: Sign in
steps.note: Account row, "Sign in on Demo Mac."

steps.text: Finish signing in in your browser.

steps.name: Open browser
steps.note: never click it in the take and never use "Copy sign-in link"; the browser page shows the account
sign-in happens off camera, then the take resumes on the signed-in card
UNVERIFIED on 0.2.6
keep the Cursor API key field ("Paste API key", "Optional. Overrides browser sign-in for this provider.") empty

shots.vo: Add the repo: the plus next to Projects, Local folder, then its path. A new chat opens. Pick Cursor in the model picker, and set Full access for this demo.

steps.name: Add project
steps.note: the + next to Projects
"New project" and "Personal assistant" rows sit above it
adding the folder opens a new chat; no separate New chat click
the model picker is labelled with the current model; UNVERIFIED for Cursor
Providers rail → Cursor, then its default model ("Auto" in source, sent to the SDK as default); UNVERIFIED

steps.name: Runtime mode
steps.note: defaults to Supervised

shots.verified: shared steps verified on 0.2.6 with Claude (episode 1); the Cursor model picker entries are not verified (Cursor reports no models until signed in)

shots.vo: Type a dollar sign, pick sw-increment, and describe the change. Cursor writes spec.md: acceptance criteria and a task with its files and test.
shots.stepChip: $ → Sw Increment → describe the change → Enter

steps.name: Message
steps.note: placeholder "Ask for changes, send follow-ups, or attach images" on a new chat
the menu lists the 11 skills title-cased: Sw Auto … Sw Team, each tagged Project Skill

steps.text: Personal greeting: greet(name) returns "Hello, <name>!" and greet() still returns "Hello, world!". Use Ada in examples. Plan only, no code yet.

steps.note: send button aria-label "Submit message"
speed-ramped in the edit, with the Sped up chip
hold on the reply: AC-01, AC-02, T-01 with its files and npm test

shots.verified: skill menu verified on 0.2.6 with Claude; Cursor's skill list is not verified

shots.vo: Then send sw-do. Cursor claims the task, changes the code, and runs the test. The task is marked done only when the test passes.
shots.stepChip: $ → Sw Do → claim → edit → test → done

steps.text: Do T-01, then stop. I will close the increment myself.

steps.note: expands the turn's steps
hold on: specweave task claim T-01, the edit to src/greeting.js, the commit with specweave task done … --run "npm test"

shots.verified: not verified for Cursor (no Cursor turn was run)

shots.vo: Click Open diff to review the code, the test, and the ledger line that records who finished the task.

steps.note: on the last turn's "5 changed files" card
the done line: "by":"cursor@demo" with its evidence
